svg.title: The six Terraform modules and the resources each one owns
svg.desc: One Terraform root calls six modules. The dns module owns the hosted zone and the mail records that travel with it, which is why its variables file is irreplaceable. The network module owns the VPC, one public subnet, an S3 gateway endpoint and the origin security group, whose only inbound rule admits CloudFront's managed prefix list; there is no SSH rule and no Postgres rule, and its single route to the whole internet is on egress. The compute module owns the one instance, its Elastic IP, the separate EBS data volume that carries the database directory, and the Systems Manager document a deploy is sent through. That document takes two image references, not a script, which is what stops the deploy role from being a root shell on the box. The app module owns the ECR repository, the media bucket, the generated secrets, every parameter the box reads at boot, the instance role and the log group. The edge module owns the certificate, validated in us-east-1, the CloudFront distribution, and the records pointing the site at it over both address families. The ci module owns the GitHub OIDC provider and the role a workflow assumes, so no AWS keys are stored in GitHub.
